title: Constructible sheaves are finitely presented; full faithfulness
statement:
Use the universe and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], with $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ as in [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_X}$, the category of internal module objects in abelian sheaves on the small pro-etale site, as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Cons}(X,\Lambda)\subset\mathcal M$ be the full subcategory of constructible sheaves of [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

Here $\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)$ denotes the ordinary ind-category: its objects are small filtered diagrams $C:I\to\mathcal C$, written $\text{“}\varinjlim_i\text{”}C_i$, and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)}(\text{“}\varinjlim_i\text{”}C_i,\text{“}\varinjlim_j\text{”}D_j)=\varprojlim_{i\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\varinjlim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(C_i,D_j),$$
with identity and composition induced by identities and composition in $\mathcal C$. Filtered diagrams and their colimits have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The use of a small skeleton of $\mathcal C$ gives the same category up to equivalence.

1. Every $C\in\mathcal C$ is finitely presented as an object of $\mathcal M$: for every small filtered diagram $(M_j)$ in $\mathcal M$, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_j\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C,M_j)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(C,\varinjlim_jM_j)$$
is bijective.
2. Sending a formal diagram $\text{“}\varinjlim_i\text{”}C_i$ to its actual colimit $\varinjlim_i C_i$ in $\mathcal M$, and sending a represented morphism $C_i\to D_j$ to its composite with $D_j\to\varinjlim_jD_j$, defines a fully faithful functor $\Phi:\operatorname{Ind}(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal M$. Its essential image is the full replete subcategory of objects isomorphic to small filtered colimits of constructible sheaves; this subcategory is denoted $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: The size convention makes the site small in the chosen enlarged universe. The sheaf tensor structure applies to abelian sheaves on precisely this small pro-etale site and supplies strong monoidal sheafification. For a presheaf map $u:F\to G$ with $a(u)$ invertible and any presheaf $P$, its natural tensor comparison identifies $a(u\otimes_p1_P)$ with $a(u)\otimes1_{aP}$, which is invertible. Thus tensoring a sheafification equivalence with a presheaf remains a sheafification equivalence, so the hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] hold. Apply that equivalence to the commutative ring object $\Lambda_X$: internal modules are equivalent to sectionwise modules over its section-ring sheaf. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] the latter category is abelian and has all small colimits. The equivalence is additive because it preserves the section maps identically; kernels, cokernels and the coimage-to-image isomorphism therefore give an abelian structure on $\mathcal M$. A cocone transported through the equivalence is universal because the Hom bijections identify its factorizations with those of the original universal cocone, giving all small colimits in $\mathcal M$. In particular every diagram appearing below has its actual colimit in the same size convention. By [det-lem-coefficient-heart-small], $\mathcal C$ has a set of isomorphism classes. Choosing representatives and taking their full subcategory gives a small skeleton; the original full category is locally small because its arrows are sheaf morphisms on the small site.

source.place: Stacks 03DA, lemma-abelian (abelian module category), and 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits (all colimits); blueprint unit sk-prop-ind-heart, step 1 (small skeleton)

proof.text: Let $C$ be constructible and $M:J\to\mathcal M$ a small filtered diagram. Regard $C$ and every $M_j$ as complexes concentrated in degree zero. They satisfy the common termwise lower bound $b=0$, and their termwise colimit is $(\varinjlim_jM_j)[0]$. The constructible-sheaf clause of [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity], with $q=0$, identifies the colimit of the derived Hom groups with the derived Hom into this termwise colimit. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] to the abelian category $\mathcal M$: its degree-zero derived Hom is ordinary module Hom. These identifications carry the cocone maps to the ordinary cocone maps, because the bijection sends $f$ to its single-complex map. Hence the displayed canonical map in assertion 1 is bijective, naturally in $C$ and the diagram. Both coefficient choices and the Noetherian hypothesis are exactly those of the cited continuity statement; no completeness or derived-colimit assertion is used.

source.place: paragraph 1; degree-zero identification: Stacks 06XS, lemma-negative-exts, part (2)

proof.text: Take small filtered diagrams $C:I\to\mathcal C$ and $D:J\to\mathcal C$, and put $A=\varinjlim_iC_i$, $B=\varinjlim_jD_j$, with cocone legs $c_i,d_j$. For each $i$, send the class of $f:C_i\to D_j$ to $d_jf:C_i\to B$. This is well-defined on the colimit of Hom sets: transition maps give equal composites by the cocone identity. For a filtered diagram of abelian groups, its set colimit carries the group operations by moving any finite list of representatives to a common stage and performing the operations there; equality is eventual equality at a common stage. Changing representatives or the chosen common stage gives the same result after a further transition: filteredness equalizes the finitely many parallel arrows involved. The group axioms hold after moving the finitely many entries of each axiom to one stage. A compatible family of group homomorphisms induces a group homomorphism on these representatives, and conversely restriction to each stage recovers that family; this proves the abelian-group colimit universal property. Thus the group-colimit comparison of step 2 is the same underlying-set comparison here. It is a bijection by step 2, since $\mathcal C$ is a full subcategory of $\mathcal M$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For a transition $t:C_i\to C_{i'}$ and a representative $f:C_{i'}\to D_j$, the two comparison maps commute with precomposition since $d_j(f t)=(d_jf)t$. Taking compatible families therefore gives a bijection between the ind Hom set in the statement and the set of compatible maps $(h_i:C_i\to B)$. The colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] bijects that latter set with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(A,B)$: send $h$ to $(hc_i)_i$, and send a compatible family to its unique factorization through $A$. These are inverse by uniqueness. Thus the Hom comparison is a bijection; this derives the contravariant colimit-to-limit formula directly, without an interchange of limits and colimits.

source.place: Stacks 05PW, remark-ind-category (Hom formula); Stacks 002F, definition-colimit (universal property); blueprint proof paragraphs 2-3

proof.text: Define $\Phi$ on objects by the chosen actual colimits and on each Hom set by the map constructed in step 3. This is exactly the claimed realization map. It preserves identities: at every $C_i$, the class represented by $1_{C_i}$ maps to $c_i$, so its induced endomorphism of $A$ is $1_A$. For composition, let $f:C\to D$ and $g:D\to T$ be ind morphisms. For each $i$, choose a representative $f_i:C_i\to D_j$ of its component, and a representative $g_j:D_j\to T_k$ of the $j$-component of $g$. Their composite represents the $i$-component of $gf$, by the ind-category composition in the statement. If $e_k:T_k\to\varinjlim_kT_k$ is a cocone leg, then $\Phi(gf)c_i=e_kg_jf_i=\Phi(g)d_jf_i=\Phi(g)\Phi(f)c_i$. Universal uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] yields $\Phi(gf)=\Phi(g)\Phi(f)$. Step 3 already makes the construction independent of all representative choices, including for general filtered categories with parallel arrows. Consequently $\Phi$ is a functor, and the bijection on every Hom set in step 3 proves it is fully faithful.

source.place: paragraph 4, expanded verification of the realization functor

proof.text: Every image object $\Phi(C)$ is an actual small filtered colimit of constructible sheaves, by its object definition. Conversely every such colimit is the image of the same diagram regarded as an ind-object. Closing these objects under isomorphism gives exactly the essential image. Since $\Phi$ is fully faithful, its image up to isomorphism is a full replete subcategory of $\mathcal M$, which is precisely the subcategory called $\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$ in the statement. This is a definition of the image, not a claim that filtered colimits preserve constructibility.
